title: Use proximity placement only for measured latency requirements
description: Benchmark before using proximity placement groups. Review compatibility with availability zones, capacity, and node-pool constraints; tighter placement can reduce placement flexibility and resilience. Do not trade away failure-domain separation without a documented reason.

documentation.title: Use proximity placement only for measured latency requirements

title: Govern cluster extensions and managed add-ons
description: Inventory installed extensions and add-ons, their supported Kubernetes versions, permissions, upgrade policies, costs, and operational owners. Remove unused components and validate lifecycle compatibility before upgrades.

documentation.title: Govern cluster extensions and managed add-ons

title: Choose a governed node resource group name at creation
description: Set a node resource group name if required by naming policy, and document AKS ownership. Its name is not a security control; protect access and avoid manually modifying AKS-managed infrastructure.

documentation.title: AKS node resource group

title: Use approved private paths for node troubleshooting
description: Keep node SSH/RDP endpoints off the public internet. Use supported AKS debug access or approved private management connectivity with time-bound permissions, audit logs, and incident ownership. Do not expose nodes merely to make troubleshooting easier.

documentation.title: Securely connect to nodes through a bastion host

title: Run supported diagnostics and configuration checks
description: Use AKS diagnostics, Azure Monitor, and maintained troubleshooting tools. Validate tool provenance and permissions before execution. Use policy and manifest validation to detect missing requests and limits; do not install an unmaintained scanner as a production prerequisite.

documentation.title: Run supported diagnostics and configuration checks

title: Enable cluster autoscaling
description: To keep up with application demands in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), you may need to adjust the number of nodes that run your workloads. The cluster autoscaler component can watch for pods in your cluster that can't be scheduled because of resource constraints.
detail: You can enable autoscaling module per node pool but only create one mutual autoscale profile

documentation.title: AKS Autoscaler
Node autoprovisioning (karpenter)
Cluster autoscaler

title: Use GitOps to deploy workloads in your cluster
description: GitOps works by using Git as a single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications
detail: On Azure you can for instance use Azure Arc for Kubernetes but also directly GitOps addon for AKS

documentation.title: Use Flux v2 addon for AKS
Use ArgoCD with AKS
What is Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes?

title: Implement CI/CD to deploy workloads in your cluster
description: Instead of GitOps (or in addition) you can use CI/CD to deploy workloads/tools in your cluster

documentation.title: Automated Deployments for Azure Kubernetes Service (Preview)
Build and deploy to Azure Kubernetes Service with Azure Pipelines
Tutorial: Deploy from GitHub to Azure Kubernetes Service using Jenkins

title: Improve efficiency with K8S Tools
description: The Kubernetes ecosystem is strengthened by many tools that make operating it easier.  Here's a few

documentation.title: OpenLens

title: Don't use the default namespace
description: It's recommended to keep all applications in a namespace other than default

documentation.title: Using multiple namespaces

title: Apply different types of labels to all resources
description: A common set of labels allows tools to work interoperably, describing objects in a common manner that all tools can understand. For instance, resources should have technical, business and security labels.

documentation.title: Recommended labels

title: Fine tune your node configuration
description: Customizing your node configuration allows you to configure or tune your operating system (OS) settings, node pools or the kubelet parameters to match the needs of the workloads.
detail: When you create an AKS cluster or add a node pool to your cluster, you can customize a subset of commonly used OS and kubelet settings.

documentation.title: Customize node configuration for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) node pools

title: Restrict command invoke on private clusters
description: AKS command invoke runs through the Azure management API and can reach a private cluster without direct network connectivity. Restrict its Azure RBAC actions, audit use, and disable it when policy requires all administration through approved private paths.

documentation.title: Restrict command invoke on private clusters

title: Consider an appropriate node size, not too large or too small
description: Optimizing node size can lead to lots of benefits including cost optimization, optimized performance and proper resource allocation

documentation.title: Which VM size should I choose as AKS node?

title: Regularly check Azure Advisor for recommendations on your cluster
description: Azure advisor can enhance environment monitoring and can help improve the operations of your cluster by reducing costs, etc

documentation.title: Azure advisor get started

title: Write manifests following good practices using dedicated tools
description: There are various tools that can make creating k8s manifest files much easier and can help with operational efficiency

documentation.title: Helm chart best practices

title: Monitor cluster certificates and verify supported rotation
description: Understand AKS-managed certificate rotation and monitor cluster health and certificate expiry. Use the documented certificate rotation procedure when necessary and assess its disruption. Workload ingress certificates need a separate renewal process.

documentation.title: Monitor cluster certificates and verify supported rotation

title: Test operational constraints before using virtual nodes
description: If using ACI-backed virtual nodes, validate monitoring, security policy, service connectivity, storage, scheduling, and application recovery end to end. Do not assume virtual nodes are equivalent to ordinary VM-backed node pools.

documentation.title: Create and configure an AKS cluster to use virtual nodes

title: Consider spot node pools for non time-sensitive workloads
description: Spot nodepools can help with cost management

documentation.title: Add an Azure Spot node pool to an AKS cluster

title: Consider subscribing to EventGrid Events for AKS automation
description: AKS emits certain events that enable it to subscribe to EventGrid which can be used for automation

documentation.title: AKS as an Event Grid source

title: Protect the AKS-managed node resource group
description: Manage nodes through supported AKS APIs and infrastructure as code, not by manually editing VM scale sets, load balancers, or networking in the node resource group. Evaluate node resource group lockdown and restrict unnecessary write access.

documentation.title: Protect the AKS-managed node resource group

title: Prepare a least-privilege incident troubleshooting workflow
description: Document diagnostics, ephemeral debug containers, log access, escalation contacts, and time-bound privileged access. Use approved images and audit actions; do not permanently install privileged debugging toolboxes across production nodes.

documentation.title: Prepare a least-privilege incident troubleshooting workflow

title: Test upgrade surge, drain timeouts, and rollback procedures
description: Before upgrading, validate regional VM quota, subnet IP space, maxSurge, PDBs, drain timeout, soak time, and deprecated APIs. Rehearse workload rollback or cluster replacement; Kubernetes control-plane downgrades are not a supported rollback strategy.

documentation.title: Test upgrade surge, drain timeouts, and rollback procedures

title: Use supported declarative APIs and validate infrastructure drift
description: Pin supported resource-provider API versions and provider/module versions. Review plan or what-if output, apply changes through code review, and detect drift. Use deployment identities scoped to the environment rather than persistent cluster-admin credentials.

documentation.title: Use supported declarative APIs and validate infrastructure drift
